original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In the exact formal group algebra F2[GL_3(F2)], with address labels restricted to the six coordinate CNOTs T_ij=I+E_ij and exactly two scalar registers, can arbitrary free scalar GL_2(F2) mixing realize diag([A],[A]) in at most five rank-one-idempotent calls, for A=T12*T13*T21? Enumerate the full 36-call alphabet (six address labels times six rank-one idempotents), using exact GL_3 group multiplication and formal coefficient vectors.
scope_change_reason: The selected card is refined to the coordinate-CNOT higher-dimensional branch left open by research/coordinate-cnot-register-bound. The target uses all three address coordinates and is distinct from that package’s two-dimensional swap/D8 target, the active third-dirty-register D8 claim, and the all-affine rank-priced PR1333 model.
bottleneck_link: A five-call word would save one paid bit operation over the direct six-call two-target word; rank(A-I)=2 gives an optimistic four-call floor. The bit supplier is not the selected binding supplier, and this abstract F2[GL_3(F2)] model has no source-bound transfer, so no kappa gain is claimed.
stop_rule: Certify the target coordinate-CNOT length in the complete 168-element Cayley graph. Exhaustively search all formal two-register words of length at most five by splitting into prefixes of length at most two and suffixes of length at most three. If a witness appears, verify exact group-algebra equality and all costs. If no witness appears, conclude minimum six only for this fixed two-register model and target. Do not expand register count or address alphabet in this cycle.
evidence: The exact replay gives GL_3(F2) order 168, target rank(A-I)=2, target CNOT length 3, and direct two-role cost 6. For all 36 paid factors, the radius-2 prefix ball has exact layers [1,36,924] (961 states) and radius-3 suffix ball [1,36,924,21112] (22073 states); 961 exact residual lookups give no word through length 5. The direct six-call identity is replayed in the full group algebra. Six omitted-call controls, a wrong-label control, a two-role single-copy positive control, a forbidden-composite-label scope control, and 252 comparisons against sparse generic matrix multiplication pass. Normal and optimized verification and package pin checks pass; no supplier or kappa gain is claimed.

open_questions.question: If the fixed two-register minimum is six, does a genuinely three-dimensional target admit a saving only after adding a restored dirty register?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current experiment settles only the smallest scalar-register boundary and cannot rule out sharing through extra roles.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one GL_3(F2) target with displacement rank below coordinate-CNOT length and build an exact bounded search for diag([A],[A],1) in the three-register formal group algebra.
open_questions.blocked_by: A 3-register generator alphabet has 168 scalar rank-one idempotents times six labels; a useful exact search needs a new pruning or meet-in-the-middle representation.

optimistic_cost_screen.experiment_threshold: At most five calls, saving at least one; no non-paid interface expense exists inside the declared abstract model.
